newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF closely monitoring September JGBs settlement.
newsitem.headline: MOF closely monitoring September JGBs settlement.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is closely monitoring the current situation regarding the delivery for September Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, a ministry official told Reuters on Monday.

Some traders said delivery of some cash JGBs against the September JGB futures contracts, scheduled for Friday next week, might fail, for the first time in history. Failure is strictly forbidden in Japan's settlement system.
Open interest in the September contract at expiry was a record 2.3519 trillion yen, the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said. The previous record was 1.6682 trillion for the March.
While an exceptionally large amount of cash JGBs are to be delivered, there is a severe shortage of the cheapest deliverable cash JGBs, traders said.
The cheapest JGBs deliverable are the 161st issue. But as the outstanding amount is only about one trillion yen, the second cheapest, the 163rd and even the 164th JGBs, have to be used for delivery.

The repo rate of the cash 161st JGBs rocketed last week, hitting more than 10 percent at one point. The September contract itself also surged before expiry, reflecting a last-ditch effort to buy back.
Some traders said United States hedge funds could be behind the huge short-squeeze in the September contract and in the deliverable cash JGBs.
Many traders said the hedge funds should have long positions on the September futures at expiry and would intend to receive much of the delivery.
One trader said he estimated the hedge funds had borrowed about 500 billion yen worth of the 161st JGB, on top of their long position of about 150 billion yen in the 161st bonds.
Their activity led to the shortage of cheapest JGBs, raising fear of failure, he added.
"We do not expect a failure of deliveries for the September as a wide range of JGBs are still available in the cash market," said a TSE official.
Deliverable cash issues are JGBs which have more than seven years but less than 11 years to maturity.
Usually, the specific issues which will be used for delivery is decided and made known to those who will receive the cash bonds about six days after the expiry, the official added.
